newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke firm after results, Hilton deal.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke firm after results, Hilton deal.

text.p: Shares in Ladbroke Group Plc were firm on Friday in a generally weaker stock market as yesterday's results and hotel deal prompted earnings upgrades, dealers said.
The shares were up 1-1/2p at 211p by 0907 GMT after touching a fresh year high of 215p following results on Thursday.
Greg Feehely, leisure analyst at Kleinwort Benson said they had issued a note on the stock last night and had raised full year forecasts to 170 million stg from 165 million stg.
"Delivering a pre-exceptional of 72.8 milion confounded many of their critics," Feehely said. "We have upgraded our forecasts again and remain buyers of the stock."
Analysts said Ladbroke's tie-up with Hilton Hotels, announced with the company's results yesterday, would also improve future profitability.
"It's a sensible deal," said Tim Baldwin, an analyst at Greig Middleton. "Forecasts will improve because there are substantial benefits from a combined marketing programme."
Feehely added the deal was more flexible than he was expecting.
"Ladbroke do not come out of it the poorer partner," he said. "The main benefits will not become apparent until 1998 onwards and there will be room for earnings upgrades."
